sections.title: From cost per tonne to tonnes per dollar
sections.explainer: charityevals' step after Giving Green's bottom line: Giving Green reports dollars per tonne; the site needs tonnes per dollar, and how much air pollution those tonnes cut. The cuts come mostly from US power plants burning less coal and gas, which emit a small fraction of the world-average smoke per tonne (docs/normalization.md 2.5). The tonnes come years after the money is spent, so they are discounted for that wait at the site's discount rate.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Giving Green's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: Total IRA climate investment
rows.explainer: The dollar amount commonly given for the IRA's climate and energy provisions when it passed in 2022.

rows.label: IRA's cumulative projected effect on emissions through 2032 (tonnes CO₂e)
rows.explainer: Princeton ZERO Lab's 2022 estimate that the IRA cuts cumulative US greenhouse gas emissions by about 6.3 billion tonnes over the decade.

rows.label: Cost-effectiveness of the IRA ($ per tonne CO₂e)
Evergreen's projected annual budget (2023)
rows.explainer: The budget Giving Green projects for 2023, written into its formula. Giving Green's deep dive says Evergreen's 2022 budget was $5 million and that it hoped to grow to $7.5 million.

rows.label: Share of Evergreen's budget going to IRA implementation
rows.explainer: Two of Evergreen's four priorities concern implementing the bill, so Giving Green puts half the budget on it. The evaluator's own subjective guess, filed as a judgment.

rows.label: Years of Evergreen's spending on IRA implementation

source.title: Giving Green, Evergreen BOTEC 2022
source.cell: Evergreen BOTEC 2022!C9 (note: "multiplied by 10 years of activity")

rows.explainer: Giving Green's sheet leaves out the ×10 that its own note and write-up describe. The sheet's formula is 0.5 × $7.5 million, one year of spending, which gives $0.49 a tonne; the note on that cell says "multiplied by 10 years of activity", and the deep dive says $3.75 million goes to implementation "each year over the next decade" and reports $4.88 a tonne, the sheet's calculation with ten years. Ten years also matches the benefit side, which applies Evergreen's influence to the IRA's whole decade of spending and emission cuts. Our view uses ten years, Giving Green's published $4.88; the evaluator view keeps the sheet's one year so its cached cells reproduce. The evaluator's own subjective guess, filed as a judgment.

rows.label: Evergreen's budget to support IRA implementation
IRA provisions that Evergreen may target
rows.explainer: The IRA line items Giving Green believes Evergreen may influence, added up on the sheet's line-items tab: about $180 billion of the $369 billion.

rows.label: Evergreen's influence on IRA implementation (share of targeted provisions)
rows.explainer: Giving Green's guess, which it calls highly uncertain and conservative given the breadth of Evergreen's influence: Evergreen's work makes 0.25% of the targeted money get spent well that otherwise wouldn't. Range is ours: Giving Green gives none; the high end is the 0.5% in its own draft tab ('scratch Evergreen BOTEC 2022'!B8), the low end a fifth of the best guess.

rows.label: IRA implementation affected by Evergreen
Emissions avoided or removed due to Evergreen (tonnes CO₂e)
rows.explainer: The IRA money Evergreen's work affects, at the IRA's average cost per tonne.

rows.label: Cost-effectiveness of Evergreen ($ per tonne CO₂e)
rows.explainer: Giving Green's bottom line. The sheet gives $0.49 a tonne; Giving Green's deep dive reports $4.88, the same calculation with ten years of spending (see "Years of Evergreen's spending"). The evaluator view reproduces the sheet; our view uses $4.88. Giving Green has low confidence in it.

rows.label: Carbon offset benchmark ($ per tonne CO₂e)
rows.explainer: Giving Green's 2022 offset benchmark, a price per tonne written as $326.40 for 19.6 tonnes.

rows.label: …is x times as cost-effective as the offset benchmark
Top recommendation benchmark ($ per tonne CO₂e)
rows.explainer: Giving Green's rough bar for a top nonprofit: about $1 a tonne, with anything under $10 plausibly in range.

rows.label: …is x times as cost-effective as the top recommendation benchmark
Years from the grant until the tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: Giving Green counts ten years of Evergreen's spending from 2023 against the Inflation Reduction Act's cuts through 2032, which grow over the decade as the money is spent on clean power and industry: on average the tonnes come a few years after the dollar that helped steer them. Our judgment from Giving Green's dates. Giving Green counts a tonne the same whenever it is avoided; the site discounts every future benefit at the discount rate under Your values, in both views (an evaluator stating dollars per tonne takes no view on discounting). The heat deaths a tonne avoids are discounted again from the year it is avoided, in the site's climate conversion.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per dollar
rows.explainer: One over Giving Green's cost per tonne, discounted for the wait until the tonnes are avoided, like every future benefit on the site. How much air pollution these tonnes cut is the rows below.

rows.label: Share of these tonnes from burning less fuel
rows.explainer: Most of the IRA's cuts come from US power plants burning less coal and gas. Set to 1 because the health studies in the next row count deaths avoided per tonne of the whole package, so the tonnes that don't come from burning less fuel are already averaged into that figure.

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths per tonne cut by US clean-electricity policy, relative to the fossil-fuel average

source.title: Energy Innovation (2022) and Resources for the Future (2022), health modelling of the Inflation Reduction Act
source.note: Deaths avoided in 2030: about 3,700–3,900 (Energy Innovation), 700–1,300 (Resources for the Future), from roughly a billion tonnes cut that year.

rows.explainer: Per fuel and place, not the world average: US power plants mostly have scrubbers. Health modelling of the Inflation Reduction Act projects about 3,700–3,900 deaths avoided in 2030 (Energy Innovation, 2022) or 700–1,300 (Resources for the Future, 2022), from roughly a billion tonnes cut that year: 0.7 to 3.9 deaths per million tonnes, 0.005 to 0.027 of the world average of 1.46 per 10,000. Best guess 0.013, the middle of the two studies' central figures on a log scale.

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
rows.explainer: The row the site's climate conversion reads (docs/normalization.md 2.5): the air-pollution deaths each of these tonnes avoids, as a multiple of the world average behind the shared rate, 1.46 air-pollution deaths per 10,000 tonnes of CO₂ from fossil fuels (Rethink Priorities). The conversion values every tonne for its heat deaths (discounted over the decades until they come) and adds "Deaths caused by one more tonne of CO₂"'s air-pollution part times this row, at once. Here: the US health studies' deaths per tonne, relative to the world average.

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths averted per tonne, counted directly by the evaluator (none here)
rows.explainer: A row every climate model has, which the site's conversion reads (docs/normalization.md 2.5): air-pollution deaths the evaluator counts itself, per tonne, on top of what the tonnes carry through air_pollution_weight. The evaluator counts none for this charity, so 0.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this charity's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Policy staff and former government officials could typically earn considerably more in law firms, consulting or lobbying. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per dollar donated
rows.explainer: The tonnes per dollar above; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest). The site turns these tonnes into years of healthy life through the deaths they avoid: "Deaths caused by one more tonne of CO₂", its heat part discounted over "Years until the heat deaths from a tonne of CO₂" for every tonne, and its air-pollution part, at once, times "Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne" above.
